ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-01-15
Provider: Dr. Aisha Johnson, MD
Department: Neurology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Daily headaches for the past 2 months that worsen with Valsalva maneuvers and associated with transient visual obscurations

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The headaches are diffuse, worsen with Valsalva maneuvers, and are associated with transient visual obscurations. She denies any history of trauma or recent illness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Her past medical history is unremarkable

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy at age 8

MEDICATIONS:
She is not taking any medications

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with chronic migraine headaches
- Maternal aunt with obesity

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1 drink per month). Occupation: Graduate student.

VITAL SIGNS:
On physical examination, her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, heart rate is 78 beats per minute, and she is afebrile

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Fundoscopic examination reveals bilateral papilledema. Neurological examination is otherwise normal.

IMAGING:
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain with and without contrast shows no abnormalities.

OTHER STUDIES:
Lumbar puncture is performed, and the opening pressure is measured at 320 mmH2O. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis is normal with no cells, normal glucose, and normal protein levels.

attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. David Chen, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Recurring, severe, throbbing headaches for 6 weeks that awaken her from sleep, with episodes of visual dimming and flashing lights when standing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient returns for emergency evaluation six months following her prior neurology consultation for similar symptoms. She presents with a 6-week history of recurring, severe, throbbing headaches that are most intense in the mornings and occasionally awaken her from sleep. She also reports brief episodes of visual dimming and flashing lights, particularly when standing up quickly. She denies vomiting, photophobia, or focal neurologic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Intracranial hypertension (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
- Tonsillectomy at age 8

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Mother with chronic migraine headaches
- Maternal aunt with obesity

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: Rare (1 drink per month). Occupation: Graduate student.

VITAL SIGNS:
She is 162 cm (5 ft 4 in) tall and weighs 88 kg (194 lb); BMI is 33.5 kg/m².

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Neurologic examination is normal except for bilateral papilledema. Pupils are equal and reactive to light. Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes, and formal visual field testing is pending.

IMAGING:
MRI of the brain is normal.
